title: SwiftUI basics: views and containers
tagline: Declarative UI, the stacks, and the controls you reach for first.
intro: SwiftUI builds apps for iPhone, iPad, Mac and Watch from one declarative description of the screen. You say what it should look like; SwiftUI works out how.

body: UIKit is imperative: you create a label, set its text and frame, and add it to a view, step by step. SwiftUI is declarative: Text("Hello") is the whole description.

blocks.caption: How a SwiftUI screen is put together.

items.label: State
items.detail: @State holds the data; changing it is the only way to change the screen
explain: @State var isOn = false declares a value SwiftUI stores for you. Writing isOn = true schedules a new body.
A control gets a binding with $: Toggle(isOn: $isOn) both reads and writes the same value.

items.label: Containers
items.detail: VStack, HStack and ZStack arrange children down, across or on top of each other
explain: VStack centres its children horizontally by default; VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 8) moves them left and spaces them.
HStack centres vertically, with .top, .center or .bottom to change it. ZStack layers children, the last one on top.

items.label: Views and modifiers
items.detail: Text, Image and Button are views; .padding() and .frame() return new, modified views
explain: Modifiers wrap rather than mutate, so order matters: .padding().background(.red) colours the padding, the reverse does not.
body is recomputed often and must be cheap: describe the view, do not load data inside it.
